article.headline: Celtic clinches first Europa League victory after hard-fought comeback against Besiktas
article.summary: Celtic secured their first win of the Europa League campaign after rallying to defeat Besiktas.
article.body:
Callum Osmand described the victory as a battle that required the team to dig in and stay strong against a high-quality opponent. The forward highlighted teammate Camilo Duran for his performance, labeling him a poacher who played an amazing role in the outcome. Osmand noted that the match atmosphere and the need to recover from an opponent's goal felt similar to their previous experience against Celta Vigo. After falling behind, the squad managed to regain their composure and find the necessary goals to secure the result.

This victory marks a significant turning point for Celtic, as it stands as the club's first win in the Europa League competition this season. For the players and coaching staff, gaining these points is essential for building momentum in the group stage standings. A successful run in European competition often defines a club's season, providing both financial benefits and a boost in team confidence that can translate into domestic league performance.

According to reports from BBC, the match featured a late push where Celtic capitalized on their opportunities to overcome Besiktas. Callum Osmand acknowledged that coming off the bench can be challenging, but he expressed satisfaction at being in the right place to contribute to the winning effort. The team’s ability to remain disciplined while trailing served as the deciding factor in the fixture.

Looking ahead, the club will aim to carry this performance into their remaining Europa League fixtures. Having finally broken their winless streak in the tournament, the players are focused on maintaining this level of consistency to improve their standing in the competition table.

article.headline: Lenny Joseph brace stuns San Siro as Ferencvaros downs AC Milan 2-0
article.summary: AC Milan suffered a damaging 2-0 defeat to Ferencvaros on Thursday, leaving the Italian side with three losses in their opening four Europa League matches.
article.body:
Lenny Joseph secured a second-half brace at the San Siro to condemn AC Milan to a 2-0 loss, a result manager Ruben Amorim described as a performance he could not explain. The defeat marks a significant low point for the hosts, who have now lost three of their first four group stage fixtures in the current European campaign.

This loss leaves AC Milan in a precarious position within the Europa League standings, threatening their progression as they struggle to maintain competitiveness on two fronts. For the club, the failure to secure points at home against Ferencvaros highlights deep-seated issues with concentration and intensity that Amorim explicitly criticized after the final whistle.

According to Goal.com, Amorim made six changes to his starting lineup following a recent victory in the Derby della Madonnina, but the gamble failed to spark the squad. Despite second-half efforts from substitute stars Luka Modric and Christian Pulisic, the home side could not bypass Ferencvaros goalkeeper Dénes Dibusz. The BBC reported that Milan players attempted several shots throughout the match, including efforts from Diego Moreira and Omari Hutchinson, but they were consistently blocked or saved.

Amorim admitted his players were not prepared to play football, stating that they surrendered the match through lack of ambition and individual mistakes. He noted that while he usually defends his team, he had no excuses for this performance. The manager identified defender Strahinja Pavlovic as the only individual whose work ethic currently meets the standards required for the team moving forward.
